text:
The scoreboard says NSH won by three, but the chances say a coin flip. Expected goals finished at 2.31 for NSH and 2.24 for STL, and the simulated replays gave NSH 51 percent to win, STL 49. The gap between that and a 5-2 result came down to goaltending and finishing. Juuse Saros stopped 24 of 26 shots, about what the chances called for, while Jordan Binnington let in five on 24 shots, 2.7 goals worse than the quality of those shots deserved.

The first period set the tone. Philip Broberg gave STL the lead at 6:21, and Jonathan Marchessault tied it on the power play at 8:40. Then Filip Forsberg wrapped one in at 12:22 on a chance worth only 3 percent. Adam Edstrom made it 3-1 with a short-handed tip-in early in the second, and Jimmy Snuggerud answered 31 seconds later on the power play. That was STL's best stretch, out-chancing NSH 0.98 to 0.36 in the period, but it produced no equalizer.

The third settled it. NSH out-chanced STL 1.03 to 0.37 in expected goals, and Ryan O'Reilly's backhand at 2:50 and Jack Drury's deflection at 8:14 closed it out. NSH also blocked 20 shots to STL's four and went 1 for 1 on the power play, while STL managed one goal on five chances. STL had more shot attempts, 57 to 44, but too many died in front of the net.
